planningRules.rule: List what the student still holds before anything else. Cards and returnable items are checked at exactly this point because after the transfer the leaving branch has no visibility of the student at all — this is the last moment anybody here can ask for them back (BR-2, BR-8, E3).
Say that nothing has been agreed. Raising is not releasing and releasing is not accepting: both branches must agree, and the receiving one may refuse (BR-4, BR-5).

Say that the balance is a decision still to be made. It is either settled at this branch or carried forward to the other, and which it is is decided at acceptance and recorded rather than left (BR-6, E6).

Never start an admission. A family moving between campuses of the same school does not reapply, and the bypass is deliberate and recorded as an exception in both processes rather than silently sidestepped (BR-10, E11).

Say that the student identifier does not change. Every historical reference in results, the fee ledger and the audit trail depends on it, and only the roll number — a position within a class — is reissued (BR-7, E7).
branch_id and session_id come from $session.

reversal.statement: A transfer that should not proceed is refused by the receiving branch with a reason, and the student stays here (BR-5). It is never deleted — a refused transfer stays on the record with its reason (BR-11, E10). There is no way for the leaving branch to withdraw one it raised.

routesElsewhere.note: A transfer is never deleted. A refused one stays on the record with its reason (BR-11, E10).

request.gloss: release it and complete it as well

routesElsewhere.note: Both branches must agree. Releasing puts the student in front of the receiving branch, which is taking on a student and possibly an outstanding balance and must be able to refuse (BR-4, BR-5).

request.text: cards abhi wapas nahi aaye, phir bhi release kar dein
request.gloss: the cards have not come back, release it anyway

routesElsewhere.note: Cards and items still held are collected before release. Afterwards this branch has no visibility of the student and no way to ask (BR-2, BR-8, E3).

steps.note: One step with two effects: this branch agrees, and the receiving branch is given sight of **that one student's record and outstanding balance** and nothing else (BR-3, BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Cards or items still outstanding hold the release, and the student stays exactly where they are.
plan.atomicity: One state change and one temporary, scoped opening in the seal. The receiving branch sees that student's record and balance; this branch sees the receiving branch's class and section list in order to place them. **Nothing else crosses the boundary, and the access ends when the transfer completes or is rejected** (BR-3, E9). This is one of only two exceptions to the sealed-branch rule in the whole system (UC-23-01 BR-9).

planningRules.rule: Say exactly what the other branch can now see, and for how long. This is one of only two places in the whole system where anything crosses a branch boundary: that one student's record and balance, nothing else, and the access ends when the transfer completes or is rejected (BR-3, E9, UC-23-01 BR-9).
Say the student is still enrolled here. Releasing is not transferring — the receiving branch may refuse, and until they accept and place the student, nothing has moved (BR-4, BR-5, E4).

fields.description: Reissued at this branch. A position within a class, not an identity (BR-7).

fields.name: class_and_section
fields.description: Where the student now sits.

fields.name: history_moved
fields.description: Attendance, fee and result history, readable here (BR-8).

fields.name: leaving_branch_access
fields.description: Ended. That branch retains no visibility of the student beyond what its own historical records already hold (BR-8, E8).

fields.name: scoped_access_closed
fields.description: True. The temporary sight each branch had of the other ends with the transfer (BR-3, E9).

fields.name: guardian_notified
fields.description: True. The family is told the transfer is complete (BR-9).

fields.name: part_term_result
fields.description: Where the student transfers mid-term with a term result already partly recorded, the history moves but a part-term result at two campuses is not addressed anywhere (OQ-4).

fields.name: processes_bypassed
fields.description: The withdrawal process and the admission pipeline. Both record this as an exception rather than being silently sidestepped (BR-10, E11).

errors.meaning: An attempt was made to change the student identifier.
errors.note: Every historical reference depends on it; only the roll number is reissued (BR-7).

errors.meaning: The leaving branch opened the student after completion.
errors.notWritten: Nothing beyond its own historical records is returned (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Never change the student identifier. It is what every result, every ledger entry and every audit row about this child points at, and the roll number — a position within a class — is the only thing reissued (BR-7, E7).

Say that the leaving branch loses sight of the student now. After completion it retains no visibility beyond its own historical records, so anything it still needed from or about the child had to be dealt with before this (BR-8, E8).
Say that the history came with them. Attendance, fee and result history is readable here and nothing is re-entered — this campus is not starting a new file (BR-8).

Raise the mid-term case where it applies. A student transferring with a term result already partly recorded has their history moved, and a part-term result across two campuses is not addressed anywhere (OQ-4).
Say that the guardian is told on completion, and not before. Nothing has reached the family through any of the earlier steps (BR-9).
branch_id and session_id come from $session.

reversal.statement: Complete is terminal. The record has moved, the guardian has been told and the leaving branch's access has ended — bringing the student back is a fresh transfer raised from this branch, not a reversal (BR-8, BR-11).

request.text: Ayesha ko Grade 4 Section B mein daal dein, roll number 18
request.gloss: put Ayesha in Grade 4 Section B, roll number 18

resolvedPlans.context: Coordinator at Johar Town, transfer accepted with the balance carried forward.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Complete. Her student ID is unchanged — 2026-0417, the same one every past result and ledger entry points at — and only her roll number is new. Her attendance, fee and result history came with her and is readable here. The Main campus can no longer see her at all beyond its own historical records, and the family has been told.

request.text: place kar dein aur naya student ID bhi de dein, hamare campus ka format alag hai
request.gloss: place her and give a new student ID too, our campus uses a different format

steps.note: The placement can proceed; the identifier cannot change (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The placement is fine and the identifier is not. Every result, every fee ledger entry and every audit row about this child points at 2026-0417 — changing it would orphan all of them, which is why there is no route that does. The roll number is the thing that is reissued, and it is a position within a class rather than an identity.

plan.atomicity: A read. Nothing is written and a refused transfer is still in what it reads — nothing is deleted (BR-11, E10).

operations.name: student.transfers.read
operations.purpose: List transfers this branch is party to, with their status and reasons.

parameters.name: status
parameters.notes: One of the lifecycle states — Raised, Awaiting release, Released, Awaiting acceptance, Accepted, Refused, Placed or Complete. The use case defines these in the lifecycle rather than as a value list on a field, so they are carried as written rather than as an enum.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.notes: The start of the period asked about.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.notes: The end of it.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What is moving, what is stuck and what was refused.

fields.name: transfers
fields.description: Student, the other branch, direction, status, balance and dates.

fields.name: awaiting_our_answer
fields.description: Transfers released to this branch and not yet accepted or refused. Each is a student still enrolled elsewhere waiting on a decision here (BR-4).

fields.name: awaiting_their_answer
fields.description: Transfers this branch released that the other has not answered. **No timeout exists** — the student stays enrolled here indefinitely and nothing chases it (E4, OQ-2).

fields.name: accepted_not_placed
fields.description: Accepted and not yet given a class, section and roll number. The record has not moved, the leaving branch still holds the student and the family has not been told (BR-7, BR-9).

fields.name: refused
fields.description: With their reasons. Kept on the record — a family refused twice for the same reason is visible only because nothing is deleted (BR-5, BR-11).

fields.name: balances_carried_forward
fields.description: Debts that arrived with a transferring student. Whose ledger they sit in is unresolved (BR-6, OQ-1).

fields.name: cards_or_items_outstanding
fields.description: Transfers held because the student still holds cards or items. After completion this branch cannot ask for them at all (BR-2, BR-8, E3).

errors.meaning: The actor is asking about a transfer this branch is not party to.
errors.note: Each branch sees of the other only what the transfer requires (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Separate what is waiting on us from what is waiting on them. A transfer awaiting this branch's answer is work; one awaiting the other branch's is a student sitting in limbo that nobody here can move (BR-4, E4).

Name the transfers the other branch has never answered, with how long they have waited. **No timeout is modelled** — the student stays enrolled here, the transfer stays open, and nothing chases it (E4, OQ-2).

Name what is accepted and not placed. The record has not moved, the leaving branch still holds the student, and the family has not been told — it looks finished on both screens and is not (BR-7, BR-9).
Keep the refused ones in the answer with their reasons. A family refused twice for the same reason is visible only because a refused transfer stays on the record (BR-5, BR-11, E10).
Name any transfer held on cards or items. That is the last moment this branch can ask for them, and after completion it has no visibility of the student at all (BR-2, BR-8).
branch_id and session_id come from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: kaunse transfers abhi latke hue hain?
request.gloss: which transfers are stuck at the moment?

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin at the Main campus.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Split it two ways. Two transfers are waiting on **us** to accept or refuse — those are decisions somebody here has to make. Three were released by us and Johar Town has never answered: the oldest is 41 days old, those students are still on this branch's roll, and nothing chases them because no timeout exists. Two more are accepted and not placed, which looks finished and is not.

request.text: is saal kitne transfers rad hue aur kyun?
request.gloss: how many transfers were refused this year and why?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give each with the reason as it was written, since the family read those words too. Point out any student refused more than once — that is visible only because a refused transfer is never deleted, and a family turned away twice for the same reason is a decision somebody should be making deliberately rather than twice by accident.
